title: The tmpfile-content assertion re-derives the expected body with the same fence …
description:
The tmpfile-content assertion re-derives the expected body with the same fence regex stripFrontmatter uses (raw.replace(/^---.../,'')). It still verifies the full read->strip->write->argv pipeline against the real agent file, so it is not tautological, but pinning a hand-written expected body (or asserting the fence markers are gone) would catch a regression in the shared regex that the current mirror cannot.

Source: cam/issue-350
Review round: 1

suggestion-fingerprint: 77b3bee56824

spec.scope:
In test/supervisor/codex-adapter.test.ts, the assertion that the codex instructions tmpfile holds the frontmatter-stripped agent body currently re-derives the expected body with the SAME fence regex stripFrontmatter uses internally (raw.replace(/^---?
[\s\S]*??
---?
?/, '')), so a regression in that shared regex would be mirrored identically by the test and pass undetected. Harden it: add an assertion that does NOT reuse the stripFrontmatter regex. Use a controlled fixture agent file (known frontmatter block + known body) written to a real tmpdir, run it through the same read->strip->write->argv path, and assert the written model_instructions_file equals a hand-pinned literal expected body. Also assert no fence markers survive (no leading '---' and no residual closing fence). Keep the existing real-agent-file pipeline assertion intact; add the fixture-based independent check alongside it.
acceptanceCriteria: A test in test/supervisor/codex-adapter.test.ts asserts the written model_instructions_file body equals a hand-written literal expected body derived from a controlled fixture (frontmatter + body), without reusing the stripFrontmatter fence regex to compute that expected value.

The hardened assertion would FAIL if stripFrontmatter's fence regex regressed (for example if it stopped stripping the closing fence), demonstrated by the expected literal being independent of the production regex.
The existing pipeline assertion against the real agent file is preserved, not deleted.
bun run typecheck, bun test, and bun run check:all all pass.
gotchas: stripFrontmatter lives in src/templates/frontmatter.ts:105; the codex adapter calls it at src/supervisor/backend-adapter.ts:373.

Do NOT reuse the /^---?
[\s\S]*??
---?
?/ regex to compute the expected body; that circularity is exactly what this issue removes.
Create the fixture agent file in a real tmpdir and hit the real read->strip->write path (patterns.md: real I/O at wire boundaries, no tautological mocks).
